summary: OUR rows 79-92 are the 14 episodes of the third OVA block, HUNTER×HUNTER G・I Final (TV 1-62, Yorknew OVA 63-70, Greed Island OVA 71-78, G.I. Final 79-92 — the conversion is confirmed by hunterpedia's per-episode 'Nth episode of the Greed Island final OVA' line, ja-WP's three separate OVA tables, AFG's '79. (01)' … '92. (14)' parentheticals and en-WP's OVA list; joined by TITLE + DVD volume + air date, never index, R20). The 13 target rows adapt ch 140-183 continuously and at ~3.4 chapters an episode, filling the gap between the stored fence anchors ep 78 → 139 [138] and ep 92 → 185 [183] with no gaps and no back-jumps: 79 → 145, 80 → 148, 81 → 151, 82 → 156, 83 → 160, 84 → 163, 85 → 166, 86 → 169, 87 → 173, 88 → 175, 89 → 178, 90 → 181, 91 → 183. Every row is canon (AFL and AFG type the whole G.I. Final block canon; the episode pages carry no anime-original blocks and no 'differences' section). The one structural surprise is the 79/80 pair: the anime front-loads all of Bisky's badlands training (from ch 142, 144 and 145) plus the Phantom Troupe's expulsion by Razor (ch 144 tail-145) into ep 79 and ends it on ch 142's Bomber reveal, holding ch 143 and ch 144's 'Release' massacre back to ep 80 — so ep 79's END (145) runs ahead of unread material and the honest resume after it is IN ch 142 (C1/C2 parity with ep 80's start). No page-level source exists for rows 79-91 (only ep 92 has one); partial-chapter markers below are derived from side-by-side synopsis comparison, not from a page count.

anchors.note: A4 END = furthest chapter reached (145: the janken/martial-arts training and Razor expelling the Troupe); A10 START = 140 (opens on the Masadora badlands march, directly after ep 78's ch 139). Ch 143 and ch 144's 'Release' massacre are NOT here — see the eps 79/80 rearranged annotation and the continue point.

A4 END = 148 (Killua wins the 288th Hunter Exam outright — the manga's ch 148 ends on the examiner announcing him the sole passer, ch 149 opens with him back at the Starting Point). START = 142 under A10: the episode opens on FIRST-TIME ch-142 pages (Jispa's attack and Little Flower), not a recap — but see flags, this tail may be ≤5 pages, in which case START = 143.

A4/A10: opens on Killua's return through the Starting Point (ch 149 p.1) and ends on Killua's Risky-Dice casino run — Rainbow Diamond, the Casino King's Fledgling Gambler, Bisky knocking him out — which is ch 151's own text; the episode's 'Gold Dust Girl' title beat is ch 150.

A4/A10: the shortest row of the block — Battera calling off the reward (ch 174) and the three-way battle opening with Genthru reaching for Gon (ch 175's last page). Both hunterpedia fields list only 174-175; the Battera cold open is ch 174's own scene, not a ch-173 recap.

anchors.note: A4/A10: resumes inside ch 181 on Genthru switching to Countdown, ends inside ch 183; ch 183's remainder (the cloaked man revealing himself to Hisoka, Gon entering the castle) is the stored ep-92 anchor's START, so this END sits exactly on the fence.

continue_points.note: Resume IN ch 142 (C1 — ep 79 stops mid-chapter on Genthru announcing the bombs; ep 80 opens on the same chapter's last pages). C3 caveat: ep 79 already showed Bisky's training from ch 144-145 and Razor expelling the Troupe (144 tail-145) ahead of this point, so those pages will re-read; ch 143 and ch 144's 'Release' massacre are still unseen and are covered by ep 80.

annotations.note: The G.I. Final opener regroups vol 15: ep 79 collects the badlands training from ch 142 (Ken/Ryu), 144 (Ryu sparring, the Troupe's boat) and 145 (Enhancement, the janken lecture, Razor's Eliminate) and then closes on ch 142's Bomber reveal, leaving ch 143 (Countdown) and ch 144's 'Release' massacre to open ep 80. Both hunterpedia directions carry the split (ep 79 Adapted = 140,141,142,144,145; ch 143 = ep 80 only).

The manga's two-stage exchange — the accomplice throwing Puhat's severed head down at the Starting Point (144) and Nickes handing the ring over OUTSIDE the game at Battera's Castle (143-144) — is condensed in the episode into one in-game meeting at the Shiso Tree grasslands, after which 'release' detonates the alliance. Basis: hunterpedia's ep-80 synopsis against the ch 143/144 synopses; no second source states the change, so treat as descriptive.

repairs.why: Stored date follows hunterpedia's 'March 7th, 2004', which is a typo: G・I Final DVD vol 3 (eps 5-6 = OUR 83-84) is dated 4月7日 by ja-WP's 各話リスト and 2004.4.7 by Nippon Animation's own goods-net DVD page, and en-WP's OVA list prints April 7, 2004. A March 7 date would also sit four days after vol 2 (2004-03-03) on a fortnightly schedule. The error still ASCENDS, so no order gate ever caught it.
Same DVD volume as ep 83 (G・I Final vol 3, 第5話/第6話) — same correction, same three sources.

structure.notes: OVA-to-row conversion used (stated per the ask): TV 1-62 (Fuji TV 1999-10-16 → 2001-03-31); OVA 1 'Yorknew City Finale' = 63-70; OVA 2 'Greed Island' = 71-78; OVA 3 'G・I Final' = 79-92, fourteen episodes across seven DVD volumes of two. Every source agrees on the block boundaries: hunterpedia's episode pages self-describe ep 78 as 'the 8th episode of the Greed Island OVA' and ep 79 as 'the 1st episode of the Greed Island final OVA'; ja-WP carries three separate OVA tables (63-70 / 71-78 / 79-92); AFG numbers the rows '79. (01)' … '92. (14)'; Nippon Animation's goods-net DVD page lists G・I Final vols 1-7 as 第1話-第14話 in exactly our title order. Rows were joined by TITLE + DVD volume + date, never by index (R20). CAUTION (G55 shape): en-WP's OVA article PROSE says Greed Island 'was made up of episodes 71 - 79' and G.I. Final 'Fourteen episodes (79 - 92)' — the 79 overlap is an error in the prose only; the article's own episode tables run 71-78 and 79-92, as does everything else. The 2011 remake has its own page family (ch 140-185 = its eps 65-75) and was not used as evidence. Chapter space = the manga's own numbering; the block's volume boundaries (v15 140-151, v16 152-163, v17 164-175, v18 176-187) match the stored boundaries exactly. Page-level splits: hunterpedia gives them only for ep 92 ('185 p. 1-11'); rows 79-91 have none anywhere, so the '(part)' markers above come from side-by-side episode/chapter synopsis comparison and should not be promoted to page ranges. Minor fence note (no repair proposed): AFG states ep 92 = 'Chapter 183, 184 and 185 (p. 1-10)' and continue at '185 (p. 11)', one page tighter than the stored '185 p.1-11'; the stored continue (185) is right either way.

flags_for_sean: ep 80 START, 142 vs 143 (A10 sliver rule): the episode opens on ch 142's closing pages (Jispa attacking Genthru, Little Flower, the explosion) — first-time material, not a recap, so I delivered START 142. If that tail is ≤5 pages the rule makes START 143 instead. No page-level source exists for this row in any language; ch 142 is 15 pages total and its Bomber-reveal section is roughly its last third.

Air-date regime for the whole OVA block: our stored dates match ja-WP's 発売日 column (2/18, 3/3, [4/7], 4/28, 6/2, 6/30, 8/18) but NOT Nippon Animation's official sell-through schedule for G・I Final (3/3, 3/17, 4/7, 5/19, 6/16, 7/14, 8/18) — the two regimes look like rental vs sell-through releases, consistently two to three weeks apart. I repaired only 83/84, where BOTH regimes say April 7 and only hunterpedia (our apparent upstream) says March 7. If Sean wants the official sell-through dates the whole 79-92 block would move; that is a separate decision.

The ep-80 'abridged' annotation (the condensed card exchange / Puhat's head) rests on hunterpedia's ep-80 synopsis alone against the manga chapters; it is descriptive colour, not an anchor input — drop it if a single-source annotation is unwanted.
